Each T_i is an intersection of closed homogeneous halfspaces and hence measurable. The finite indicator sum is at least one everywhere, so the exact overlap identity and averaging bound hold with all overlaps included.
A menu containing a nonzero functional confines its protecting cone to a central halfspace of Gaussian mass one half. A one-cone cover consequently has only the zero functional in its menu.

In a minimal two-cone cover both cones are proper; each has mass at most one half, and union mass one forces equality and null overlap. A closed subset of its confining halfspace missing an interior point misses a positive Gaussian open set; closure then recovers the boundary. Two central closed halfspaces cover exactly when their oriented inward normals are opposite multiples. Nonnegative covectors on a halfspace must vanish on its boundary hyperplane and lie on the inward nonnegative ray.

In dimension two the s equal sectors of angle 2π/s are convex for s≥2 and are given by homogeneous halfspaces. Gaussian rotation invariance gives mass 1/s, with boundary rays null. This proves sharpness over abstract protecting-cone systems.
